intro: Looking for a life insurance advisor near you usually means you want someone local to talk through how your family would manage financially if you weren't around. Perhaps you've just taken on a mortgage, had a child, or started supporting a partner or parent. A life insurance adviser can recommend term, decreasing or whole-of-life cover to protect the people who depend on you.
need_heading: What people searching for a local life insurance advisor usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for a life insurance advisor near me are trying to put sensible protection in place and want a real person they can speak to face to face.
needs: You have taken on a mortgage or other significant debt and want cover that would help your family keep up the payments if you died.
You have children or other dependants and want to make sure they would be provided for financially.
You are unsure whether term, decreasing or whole-of-life cover suits your situation and want it explained clearly.
You want to understand how a policy could be written in trust so any payout goes to the right people without unnecessary delay.
You have had a big change such as a new job, a house move, a separation or a new baby and want your existing cover looked at again.
context_heading: Checking who you are dealing with
context: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

A good adviser will take time to understand your demands and needs, explain the key features and exclusions of any policy, and tell you how they are paid. If something goes wrong and a complaint is not resolved, you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Because quotes are price on application, ask each adviser to set out their costs clearly before you commit.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say roughly where you live so we can introduce you to a professional who covers your area.
Explain who you want to protect, such as a partner, children or other dependants.
Mention any debts or mortgage you want the cover to sit alongside.
Describe whether you are looking for new cover or a fresh look at an existing policy.
Say whether you already have cover written in trust and whether you understand how it works.
Note any preferences you have, such as speaking to someone face to face or dealing with a Chartered firm.
questions: How are you paid for arranging my cover, and will you set that out in writing?
Would term, decreasing or whole-of-life cover best match my debts and needs?
Should this policy be written in trust, and what would that involve?
What are the key exclusions and limitations I should understand before I decide?
When should I look at this cover again after a big change in my circumstances?
Are you authorised by the FCA or an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and how can I check?

faqs.q: What does a life insurance advisor actually do?
faqs.a: A life insurance adviser recommends term, decreasing or whole-of-life cover to protect your dependants. They should look at your debts and needs, explain the key features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.

faqs.q: How do I check that an advisor is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check them on the FCA register before you go ahead, and many also belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association.

faqs.q: Why might a policy be written in trust?
faqs.a: Writing a policy in trust can help any payout reach the people you intend without unnecessary delay. Ask your adviser to explain how it would work for your circumstances and whether it suits the cover you choose.

faqs.q: What should I do if I am unhappy with the advice?
faqs.a: Raise the complaint with the firm first, as they should have a clear process for handling it. If it is not resolved to your satisfaction, you can take the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

extra_heading: What happens at a first meeting with a local life insurance adviser
extra: A first meeting with a life insurance adviser is mostly a conversation about your circumstances rather than a sales pitch. Expect them to ask about your mortgage and other debts, who depends on your income, and what you would want any payout to cover. They should also explain how they are paid before you go any further, so you can decide whether to carry on.

The adviser will then talk you through the main types of cover — term, decreasing and whole-of-life — and how each might line up with your debts and needs. This is the moment to ask about writing the policy in trust, because that decision affects who receives the money and how quickly. Take your time, ask for anything unclear to be repeated, and do not feel pressured to decide on the day.

Before the meeting ends, ask what happens next and whether you will receive anything in writing setting out the recommendation and the costs. It also helps to ask when you should come back for a review, particularly after a big change such as a new mortgage, a separation or a new child. A good adviser will welcome those questions rather than brush them aside.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to have my mortgage details ready before I speak to a local adviser?
extra_faqs.a: It helps to know the rough size of your mortgage and any other significant debts, because the adviser will use that to match cover to your needs. You do not need exact figures to start the conversation, but having the paperwork nearby makes the first meeting more useful.

extra_faqs.q: Is a local life insurance adviser different from a general insurance broker?
extra_faqs.a: A general insurance broker may deal with home, car or business cover, while a life insurance adviser focuses on protection for your dependants through term, decreasing or whole-of-life policies. If you want both sorts of cover, say so when you enquire so we can introduce you to someone who handles what you need.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to an adviser face to face rather than only by phone?
extra_faqs.a: Many people search for a life insurance advisor near me because they would rather talk things through in person. Tell us roughly where you live and whether a face-to-face meeting matters to you, and we will introduce you to a professional who covers your area.
